title: The Room and the Raid: eleven years in Florence, and a frontier painted at second hand
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Palermo, the father's commissions for Rosas
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the father's Rosas-era commissions are attested but no structure and no dates are named, and Palermo is the standard identification of Rosas's Buenos Aires seat, not a documented site of this family's work
stops.campa: Before the son paints anything, the father builds. He works under commission from Juan Manuel de Rosas, whose quinta at Palermo holds the governor's court apart from the city he rules: low white galleries, water ditches, orange trees on the flats by the river. Walls go up for a man whose armies are pushing at a frontier a thousand miles south, and the work is measured in courses of brick, not in politics. Decades later the son will paint that frontier as legend, at a distance, out of reading. The father only ever closed a roof over it.
suggested_refs: The Rosas quinta at Palermo, on the ground of today's Parque Tres de Febrero

stops.name: Buenos Aires, born in the year of Caseros
stops.date_confidence: attested by es.wikipedia; a Wikidata statement field has returned 1855, and the 1852 reading is followed here as the majority one
stops.campa: Ángel della Valle is born in Buenos Aires on the tenth of October, 1852, the year Rosas falls at Caseros and the provinces begin arguing again about what a nation is. His father is a builder, a constructor of walls who has raised buildings in this city on commission from Rosas himself. Eight months after the governor rides out of the country, the builder's household goes on measuring a life in correct proportion. The capital around the boy is colonial in its bones and keeps no academy of painting. Whatever he becomes, he will have to cross an ocean to learn it.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires in the year of Caseros, 1852, a capital with no art academy

stops.name: Colegio San José, the schooling of a builder's son
stops.date_confidence: inferred: attendance at the Colegio San José is attested, but no source gives the years
stops.campa: The boy sits out his schooling at the Colegio San José on Azcuénaga, in Balvanera, one of the few classrooms a Buenos Aires family of means can choose. The curriculum is letters and Latin, not line; nothing in it points at paint. What these years give him instead is Pedro Lagleyze, a friend of his childhood who will grow into an ophthalmologist with the president of the republic among his patients. The school teaches him nothing of his trade. It gives him the man who will one day put him in a room with Julio Argentino Roca.
suggested_refs: The Colegio San José, Azcuénaga 158, Balvanera, Buenos Aires
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Colegio San José (Buenos Aires)' for the address and coordinates

segments.name: The Crossing and the Florentine Discipline

stops.name: Puerto de Buenos Aires, embarkation for Italy
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the source says only that he went to Italy at twenty, and no port, ship or month is named anywhere
stops.campa: At twenty he leaves. The city has no academy that can carry him further, only private masters working alone, and what he wants is Florence, Ciseri, the oil technique nobody here can teach. He boards in the rough anchorage on the Río de la Plata that serves this capital as a port, decades before Madero's docks and breakwaters exist, lighters ferrying passengers out to deep water. He leaves behind a builder's household and a country ten years out of its civil war, and he will learn Italian first as a language of paint. He does not come back for eleven years.
suggested_refs: The pre-Madero anchorage of Buenos Aires, in use for River Plate passenger crossings until the 1890s

stops.name: Porto di Genova, the landfall
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: no source names his port of arrival, and Genoa is offered as the standard nineteenth-century landfall for River Plate passenger routes
stops.campa: He lands at Genoa, the port every River Plate steamer answers to, the gate through which so much of Buenos Aires arrived travelling the other way. Ligurian terraces climb behind the mole and ships from every Mediterranean harbour crowd the water. He does not stay. This is the last salt water before an interior he has never seen, in a country whose language he holds by descent rather than by habit. He turns inland toward Tuscany, toward a studio he has never entered and a master he knows only by report.
suggested_refs: Genoa as the standard European landfall of the River Plate steamer routes

stops.name: Florence, the studio of Antonio Ciseri
stops.date_confidence: attested that he studied in Florence under Ciseri from about 1872 until 1883; the month and the exact premises are not recorded
stops.campa: In Florence he finds what Buenos Aires could not give him: Antonio Ciseri, the Swiss-Italian master teaching senior technique here, precise to the point of severity, a painter who builds a face the way an anatomist builds a body. Della Valle stays eleven years, the longest stretch of study in his life. He learns to lay oil as Ciseri lays it, layer over glazed layer, with nothing surrendered to haste. The method comes home in his hands intact, and every Argentine picture he has not yet imagined will be built out of it.
suggested_refs: Antonio Ciseri's teaching studio and the Accademia di Belle Arti di Firenze

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Sociedad Estímulo founded without him
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the founding; della Valle is in Italy and has no part in it
stops.campa: On the twenty-third of October, while della Valle is grinding through his Tuscan years, a circle of young men founds the Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes to give Buenos Aires the art teaching it has never had: Eduardo Sívori and his brother Alejandro, Eduardo Schiaffino, Santiago Vaca Guzmán, Alfred Paris, the architect Julio Dormal, the journalist Carlos Gutiérrez, Giuseppe Agujari. The painter and lithographer Juan Camaña takes the chair. The institution that will employ him for eighteen years, and in whose lesson he will die, exists before he has heard of it.
suggested_refs: The founding of the Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes, 23 October 1876

stops.name: Venice, the bronze horses of San Marco
stops.date_confidence: the painting and its 1881 date are attested in the work list; that he executed it in Venice before the basilica, rather than from prints elsewhere in Italy, is inferred from the title
stops.campa: He goes north to Venice and paints Caballos de San Marcos before the four bronze horses over the door of the basilica. The horses have a long raid behind them: looted out of Constantinople in 1204, set on this facade in the thirteenth century, carried off by Napoleon to Paris and brought back in 1815. Della Valle studies them as pure form, four animals held mid-stride in gilded bronze, and files the motion away. Eleven years later other horses will cross a river at the gallop on a canvas of his own.
suggested_refs: The Horses of Saint Mark, Basilica di San Marco, Venice

segments.name: The Return and the Room in His Parents' House

stops.name: Puerto de Buenos Aires, the return
stops.date_confidence: the 1883 return is attested in both the Spanish and English articles; the port, the month and the vessel are reconstruction
stops.campa: He comes back in 1883 by the same anchorage he left from, eleven years older, trained in a technique no one in this city can match. Buenos Aires has changed less than he has. It is still a capital without an academy, still importing its skill, and for the moment he is one of the imports. He carries Ciseri's glazes and Florence's patience in his hands and nowhere to put them but his parents' house. The crossing is over. The career that will make his name has not started yet.
suggested_refs: The 1883 return, given in es.wikipedia as 'En 1883 volvió a Argentina'

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the easel in his parents' house
stops.date_confidence: attested that he installed his studio in his parents' house on returning in 1883; no source gives the address, so this stop falls back to the city pin
stops.campa: Home, he sets his easel up inside his parents' house. No rented atelier, no separate address, a room in the household that raised him given over to paint. Nearly everything he is remembered for gets made here: the pampa, the gauchos, the grass fires, the raid. His father built to commission for a man who spent his life trying to shut the southern frontier. The son paints that frontier from a room in the capital, at second hand, out of reading and invention, and the country accepts the invention as memory.
suggested_refs: The della Valle family house in Buenos Aires, address unrecorded

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the circle of the generation of 1880
stops.date_confidence: the names are attested as his circle, the date is not: de la Cárcova was seventeen in 1883 and Cafferata died in 1890, and the only documented assembly of the group is the 1893 photograph, so read this as c.1883-1893
stops.campa: He falls in with the generation coming up around him: Eduardo Sívori, Augusto Ballerini, Lucio Correa Morales, Francisco Cafferata, Ernesto de la Cárcova, Reinaldo Giudici, Eduardo Schiaffino. Painters and sculptors, most of them trained in Europe or bound for it, trying to build an Argentine art out of European schooling. They are not a movement and they have no salon to hang in. They are a dozen men in one city who know what a picture costs to make, and within twenty years they hold the museum, the academy and the national commissions.
suggested_refs: The Buenos Aires painters and sculptors of the 1880s, later the founders of the national art institutions

stops.name: Buenos Aires, taken on to teach drawing
stops.date_confidence: the eighteen years of drawing teaching at the Sociedad Estímulo are attested, the starting year is not given and is inferred from the 1883 return
stops.campa: He is taken on at the Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes to teach drawing, three sessions a week, with Reinaldo Giudici beside him in the drawing and painting workshop. He holds the post eighteen years. This is the ordinary labor under the famous canvas: charcoal, plaster casts, the human figure broken into planes, the same corrections repeated to boys who will still be painting long after he is dead. The country has no state art school yet. What it will later call its academy starts as this room and these three sessions a week.
stops.quote: Ángel della Valle y Reinaldo Giudici en Dibujo y Pintura
stops.quote_source: es.wikipedia.org, 'Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes', on the educators incorporated into the academy's workshop
suggested_refs: The drawing and painting workshop of the Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes

stops.name: Casa Rosada, the portrait of the president
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: the Lagleyze connection and the Roca portrait are attested, the year is not recorded, and no source places the sitting at the Casa de Gobierno rather than a private house or the painter's own room
stops.campa: Pedro Lagleyze, the friend of his childhood, is by now an eye doctor whose patients include Julio Argentino Roca, president of the republic and the general who commanded the campaign that emptied the southern frontier. Through the doctor the painter is brought before the president, and della Valle paints him. A consulting room turns out to be the antechamber of a state commission. The face he sets down is the face of the man who ordered the southern campaign, and the introduction came from a childhood friend who treated the general's eyes.
suggested_refs: The della Valle portrait of Julio Argentino Roca

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the pampa sold by the frame
stops.date_confidence: the titles and years are attested in the es.wikipedia work list; the studio setting is inferred from his documented working method
stops.campa: The subjects arrive out of the same room, year after year. Tren de La Pampa in 1888, a train laid across open country. Anochecer en la laguna in 1889, dusk standing on still water. La diosa del Amor in 1890. He is painting a republic that is laying track at speed, filling with immigrants off the same steamers he crossed on, and buying pictures of the countryside to hang on city walls. The pampa reaches Buenos Aires as canvas, framed, at exactly the moment the railway is making it a place you could go and see.
suggested_refs: Tren de La Pampa (1888), Anochecer en la laguna (1889), La diosa del Amor (1890)

segments.name: The Raid: a Frontier Invented in a City Room

stops.name: Choele Choel, the frontier closed by clearing it
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for Roca's letter from Choele Choel; della Valle is not present and never travels here
stops.campa: Thirteen years before the picture, some six hundred miles south of the studio, Julio Argentino Roca's columns reach the Río Negro at Choele Choel and the campaign called the Conquest of the Desert closes the frontier by emptying it: tribes broken, caciques taken, land surveyed and sold to men who never rode it. The malón, the mounted raid that terrified the frontier settlements for a century, ends here as a military fact. What survives it is the image. Della Valle paints the raid in 1892, when the thing itself has been finished for seven years and can be safely remembered.
suggested_refs: Roca's Río Negro campaign of 1879 and the letter from Choele Choel, 2 June 1879

stops.name: Buenos Aires, La vuelta del Malón painted
stops.date_confidence: the 1892 date, the medium and the dimensions 186.5 by 292 cm come from the painting's own article; della Valle's own article gives 192 by 131 cm, a contradiction left standing
stops.campa: In the family room he paints the picture that outlasts everything else he makes. La vuelta del Malón: raiders crossing water at the gallop in the last light, a captive woman slung across a horse, church silver glinting among the plunder, dust and horseflesh rendered with the exact glazed patience Ciseri drilled into him in Florence. Oil on canvas, 186.5 by 292 centimetres. It is the first large-format Argentine painting to take the indigenous raid as its subject, and it fixes for a century how the country pictures a thing most of the country never saw.
stops.quote: Fue el primer cuadro pintado en gran formato que representó la temática indígena en Argentina
stops.quote_source: es.wikipedia.org, 'La vuelta del malón' (uncited assertion in the article body, not a museum statement)
suggested_refs: La vuelta del Malón, 1892, oil on canvas, Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the bazaar of Nocetti y Repetto
stops.date_confidence: the bazaar showing is attested, the month is not recorded, and the street is unnamed in the source
stops.campa: The painting is first shown in a shop. There are no salons and no art galleries in the city yet, so the largest canvas anyone in Buenos Aires has painted goes on display at the Nocetti y Repetto bazaar, among the ordinary commerce of a retail block, and people come in off the street to look at it between errands. The frontier hangs where the city buys its crockery and its lamp oil. Within a year the same canvas is representing the republic on another continent.
stops.quote: en el bazar Nocetti y Repetto, ya que no existían aún en la ciudad salones ni galerías de arte
suggested_refs: The Nocetti y Repetto bazaar, Buenos Aires, first exhibition site of La vuelta del Malón

stops.name: Jackson Park, Chicago, the canvas travels alone
stops.date_confidence: the Chicago showing in the Argentine section is attested; the month is taken from the exposition's own opening and no source records della Valle crossing with the painting
stops.campa: The canvas crosses an ocean without its painter. It hangs in the Argentine section of the World's Columbian Exposition at Jackson Park, one picture inside a temporary white city built to announce the New World to itself. Della Valle stays in Buenos Aires. The painting travels as a proxy for a nation explaining itself to visitors who have never crossed the pampa or heard the word malón: raiders and captives rendered in a technique learned in Florence, applied to a subject no Florentine master ever thought to paint.
suggested_refs: The Argentine pavilion at the World's Columbian Exposition, Chicago, 1893

segments.name: The Teacher and the Last Decade

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the group photograph of 1893
stops.date_confidence: the photograph is dated 1893 in its caption; the month, the photographer and the room are not recorded, and no source names the premises
stops.campa: A photographer sits the Sociedad's men down for a group portrait. Seated: Eduardo Schiaffino, Eduardo Sívori, Ernesto de la Cárcova, Augusto Ballerini, Martín L. Boneo. Standing: Ángel della Valle, Lucio Correa Morales, Américo Bonetti. Eight men who between them will make a national museum, a national art school, and a good part of what hangs in both. It has the look of a class photograph. It is closer to a founding board, caught three years before the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes opens its doors.
stops.quote: De izquierda a derecha, sentados: Eduardo Schiaffino, Eduardo Sívori, Ernesto de la Cárcova, Augusto Ballerini y Martín L. Boneo; parados: Ángel della Valle, Lucio Correa Morales y Américo Bonetti. (1893)
stops.quote_source: es.wikipedia.org, 'Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes', caption to the 1893 group photograph
suggested_refs: The 1893 group photograph of the Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes

stops.name: Lomas de Zamora, the station on the southern line
stops.date_confidence: the title and year are attested in the work list; whether he worked trackside or from sketches afterward is not recorded anywhere
stops.campa: He paints the station at Lomas de Zamora, a real platform on a real line running south out of the capital, one of the towns the railway stitched onto Buenos Aires as the city outgrew its edges. After the invented frontier of the Malón the geography here is exact: any traveller of the period could name the place and give the hour of the train. He is painting a timetable, steam and iron laid across the same flat country he elsewhere paints as wild and unclosed.
suggested_refs: Estación de Lomas de Zamora, 1893

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the ring race painted from town
stops.date_confidence: the title and 1893 date are attested; the month is arbitrary and the studio setting is assumed from his documented working method, not attested for this canvas
stops.campa: He paints the ring race: criollo riders spurring at a small ring hung above the track, lance tips raised, a game of the estancias and the pulperías rendered with a city painter's exactness. The countryside reaches him as material rather than as weather. By 1893 he can choose his subjects from a settled position, and he chooses the gaucho as spectacle, skill staged for an audience that meets the campo in frames like this one. The buyers hanging it have mostly never watched a horse cut a herd.
suggested_refs: Corrida de Sortija, 1893

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the edge of the monte
stops.date_confidence: the title and 1895 date are attested; the depicted ground is generic scrubland with no identifiable site, and the studio setting is inferred rather than documented
stops.campa: Al borde del monte, the edge of the scrub, the threshold where worked land gives out and the wilder growth begins. He has spent more than a decade painting a country he mostly reaches through study. The edge of the monte is his own working position as much as his subject: a city painter standing at the border of a rural world he renders with total confidence and partial acquaintance, in the exact years when that world is being fenced, ploughed, and sold off behind the picture plane.
suggested_refs: Al borde del monte, 1895

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the names in the classroom
stops.date_confidence: the students are attested by surname only, Boggio, Daneri and Victorica, with no years given; the identification of Victorica as Miguel Carlos and Daneri as Eugenio is inference, and no article was found for a painter named Boggio
stops.campa: The names in his classroom outlast most of his canvases. Boggio, Daneri and Victorica come through the Sociedad's drawing rooms under his correction, and Victorica will paint the tenement courtyards and pierrots of La Boca long after the pampa pictures have gone quiet. He is teaching, without knowing it, the generation that will refuse his subjects. He crossed an ocean at twenty because there was no one here to teach him. The boys under his correction can stay where they were born and still learn the trade.
suggested_refs: Miguel Carlos Victorica and Eugenio Daneri, pupils of the Sociedad Estímulo drawing rooms

stops.name: Buenos Aires, fire on the pampa
stops.date_confidence: the title and 1900 date are attested in the work list; the studio setting is inferred, and the scene described here is the subject named by the title, not a documented description of the canvas
stops.campa: Grass fire on the open pampa, worked at the scale Florence taught him to command. Incendio en La Pampa belongs to the last productive stretch of his life, made in the room he has painted in for seventeen years. The subject needs no journey to reach: fire on a horizon, smoke flattening under wind, a landscape reduced to its most legible danger. The men who fight grass fires do it with wet hides and firebreaks, hundreds of miles from here. He paints the thing from an address he has not moved from in seventeen years.
suggested_refs: Incendio en La Pampa, 1900

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the gaucho at work
stops.date_confidence: the title and 1900 date are attested; the month is arbitrary and the studio setting is inferred from his working pattern
stops.campa: Apartando: cattle cut out of the herd, the daily labor of ranching country, painted with the same patient glaze he learned watching Ciseri build a face. The gaucho at work rather than the gaucho at war. No captives, no raid, no burning horizon, only a man and a horse doing the job the estancias run on, for an urban audience that consumes the campo through canvases. He is forty-seven, most of a career spent inside one city, still turning out the countryside from a studio that has never moved an inch.
suggested_refs: Apartando, 1900

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the studio painted from inside
stops.date_confidence: the title and 1900 date are attested; the month is arbitrary and no description of the canvas was found in any reachable source
stops.campa: El taller: the studio itself becomes the subject. After seventeen years of pampas and raids and railway stations made at this address, he turns the picture inward and paints the workspace. Brushes, canvas, north light, the props of a trade. This is where the Argentina he is famous for actually gets built, at an easel, in a house, in the middle of a capital. A self-portrait with the self left out, only the room that stood in for every place he never went. He has three years to live.
suggested_refs: El taller, 1900

segments.name: The Class That Did Not Finish

stops.name: Buenos Aires, death in the middle of a lesson
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day in both the Spanish and English articles; the room is not specified beyond the fact that he was teaching
stops.campa: On the sixteenth of July, 1903, death takes him while he is giving a class. He is fifty years old, eighteen years into teaching drawing three times a week, and he goes down in front of his students in the middle of a correction. There is no deathbed and no farewell. A teacher stops mid-sentence and the lesson ends. His last three canvases are three years behind him, and one of them is the room he made them in. The Argentina he invented inside his parents' house has already crossed to Chicago without him.
stops.quote: la muerte lo sorprendió el 16 de julio de 1903, mientras estaba dictando clases
suggested_refs: The drawing classroom of the Sociedad Estímulo de Bellas Artes, July 1903

stops.name: Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Room 24
stops.date_confidence: the museum reached this Recoleta building in 1932 and the painting hangs in Room 24 today; no source consulted dates the acquisition of the canvas, and the museum's own site returned HTTP 403
stops.campa: La vuelta del Malón hangs in Room 24 of the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes on Avenida del Libertador, among the nineteenth-century Argentine painting. The museum was created by decree in 1895 with Eduardo Schiaffino, who stood beside him in the 1893 photograph, as its first director. It opened in the Bon Marché on Florida in 1896, moved to the Pabellón Argentino in 1909, and reached this remodelled pump house in 1932. What began as a bazaar-window attraction ends on a national wall.
suggested_refs: Sala 24, Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, Av. del Libertador 1473, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Diagonal Sur y Perú, the argument in bronze
stops.date_confidence: the monument's 1941 erection and the vandalism from 2005 onward are attested; della Valle has been dead thirty-eight years when the bronze goes up
stops.campa: Four blocks from where the painter kept his easel, a bronze Julio Argentino Roca goes up in 1941: the general who closed the southern frontier, cast at the civic core of the city that banked the profit. From 2005 the plinth starts collecting paint. Roca genocida. The same argument reaches the museum wall a few kilometres north, where the raiders in the canvas ride out of a country the campaign had already emptied. Painted, the raid was the thing being feared. Read now, it is the alibi of the men who did the clearing.
stops.quote_source: Graffiti on the Roca monument, Buenos Aires, from 2005 onward, per julio_argentino_roca.journey.json
suggested_refs: The Roca monument at Diagonal Sur and Perú, erected 1941

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the canvas read as evidence
stops.date_confidence: the article's outlet and date are attested through a secondary summary; the original text could not be reached and no direct quotation from it was available
stops.campa: A hundred and twenty-nine years after the canvas, a Buenos Aires newspaper runs a survey of what it calls the problem of the Indian in River Plate painting and files della Valle alongside Raymond Monvoisin, Johann Moritz Rugendas and Juan Manuel Blanes: the men who supplied the images by which a nation under construction pictured the people it was clearing off the land. The painting is no longer read as a scene. It is read as evidence of a founding imagination, still hanging in Room 24 where anyone can go and argue with it.
suggested_refs: Página/12, 'Una mirada al problema del indio en la pintura rioplatense', 31 October 2021
sources: Página/12 (2021-10-31), reached only through an infobae.com summary of the piece
